title: Criticality of a join of graphs
statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on finite, nonempty, disjoint vertex sets, and let $G \vee H$ denote their join, the graph obtained from the disjoint union of $G$ and $H$ by adding an edge between every vertex of $G$ and every vertex of $H$. Recall that a graph is \emph{critical} when every proper subgraph has strictly smaller chromatic number than the graph itself. Then $G \vee H$ is critical if and only if both $G$ and $H$ are critical.
hypotheses_covered: G is a simple graph on a finite vertex set
H is a simple graph on a finite vertex set
the vertex set of G is nonempty
the vertex set of H is nonempty
replaced:

and only if both \texttt{G$_{1}$} and \texttt{G$_{2}$} are critical.}
